claims.text: In situ formation of an ultra-nanocrystalline surface layer is the key mediator of simultaneous wear and corrosion resistance in high-entropy alloys.
Dynamic surface nanostructuring reduces friction and wear through grain-boundary strengthening.
Dynamic surface nanostructuring promotes formation and adherence of a protective oxide layer.
The relevant as-processed high-entropy alloy has a relatively coarse initial grain structure.
Mechanical loading induces near-surface grain refinement through dynamic amorphization.
Wear cycles produce an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer with a high density of grain boundaries.
The ultra-fine near-surface layer lowers friction and limits material removal.
Refined surface grain boundaries provide abundant and stable nucleation sites for a protective oxide film.
The oxide film formed on the refined surface is more adherent and resistant to breakdown, thereby reducing corrosion.
The coupled wear-reduction and passive-film-stabilization effects govern resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
An alloy that develops the dynamic ultra-nanostructured surface will have a lower wear rate than a baseline lacking that surface.
An alloy that develops the dynamic ultra-nanostructured surface will have a lower corrosion current density than a baseline lacking that surface.
Wear volume, friction coefficient, and corrosion rate may decrease by approximately 30–50%.
The proposed benefit requires mechanical deformation sufficient to induce dynamic surface nanocrystallization.
The proposed benefit requires a corrosive medium capable of forming a passive film on the refined grain boundaries.
The benefit will fail or weaken when mechanical stresses are too low to trigger nanocrystallization.
The benefit will fail or weaken in environments aggressive enough to rapidly compromise the passive film.
The magnitude of the effect varies with alloy composition, deformation mode, and corrosive species.
A thermal treatment or surface coating can inhibit surface grain refinement without otherwise altering the relevant wear and corrosion response.
Similar or superior wear and corrosion resistance in the group lacking the nanocrystalline layer would falsify the claim that the layer is the key mediator.

contradictions.description: The baseline is inconsistently defined as either a sample exposed to only one stress or a sample exposed to the same combined stresses with nanocrystallization inhibited. A single-stress sample is not a matched control for combined tribocorrosion and cannot isolate the proposed mediator.
